description: Evaluation cases for the static-site skill. Tests whether agents produce correct @dfinity/static-site (certified-assets) configuration — _redirects SPA rules, _headers, recipe setup — avoid legacy .ic-assets.json5 / AssetManager on the new canister, and handle migration from the legacy asset canister.

output_evals.name: Static-site recipe setup
output_evals.prompt: Show me the icp.yaml configuration to deploy my Vite frontend on the IC with the recommended certified-assets recipe, including the build step. Just the YAML and the deploy command — no _headers, no _redirects, no programmatic upload code.
expected_behaviors: Uses the @dfinity/static-site recipe (certified-assets), not @dfinity/asset-canister
Sets dir: dist (Vite output)
Includes build commands (e.g. npm ci / npm install, npm run build)
Uses icp deploy, NOT dfx deploy

output_evals.name: SPA routing on static-site uses _redirects, not .ic-assets.json5
output_evals.prompt: I'm hosting my React SPA on the IC with the @dfinity/static-site recipe. Refreshing a deep route like /dashboard/settings returns 404. How do I fix it? Just the config file and where it goes.
expected_behaviors: Adds a _redirects file at the root of the build/dir directory
Uses the rule /*  /index.html  200 (a rewrite, status 200)
Does NOT use .ic-assets.json5 or enable_aliasing (those are the legacy asset canister)
Does NOT use a 301/302 redirect for the SPA fallback

output_evals.name: Adversarial: AssetManager does not work on certified-assets
output_evals.prompt: I deployed my frontend with the @dfinity/static-site recipe. Write me a Node.js script that uses AssetManager from @icp-sdk/canisters to upload an extra file to it.
expected_behaviors: Explains that AssetManager targets the legacy SDK asset canister and does NOT work against the certified-assets (static-site) canister
States that static-site uploads happen through the recipe's sync plugin on icp deploy (different upload API: upload_chunks/execute_operations)
Does NOT present AssetManager.store() as a working way to upload to a static-site canister
Points the user to the legacy @dfinity/asset-canister recipe if they genuinely need programmatic AssetManager uploads

output_evals.name: Custom headers / CSP via _headers (no defaults)
output_evals.prompt: How do I set a Content-Security-Policy and cache headers on my @dfinity/static-site frontend on the IC? Just the config file and the key rules.
expected_behaviors: Uses a _headers file at the root of the dir (Netlify-style syntax)
Notes the certified-assets canister adds NO default headers, so you must declare them
Explains patterns match the file/asset key (e.g. /index.html, /*.html), not the visitor URL
Does NOT use .ic-assets.json5 or a security_policy field

output_evals.name: Adversarial: migrating asset-canister to static-site requires reinstall
output_evals.prompt: I'm migrating my existing @dfinity/asset-canister frontend to the @dfinity/static-site recipe. I just changed the recipe type and ran icp deploy but it failed. What's the gotcha? Just the key points.
expected_behaviors: Explains the two canisters have incompatible stable-memory layouts, so an in-place upgrade fails/panics
Recommends icp deploy --mode reinstall (which wipes state and re-syncs) or deploying a fresh canister
Mentions converting .ic-assets.json5 to _headers/_redirects as part of the migration
Does NOT claim a plain icp deploy upgrade works across the two recipes

output_evals.name: Legacy asset canister SPA still supported
output_evals.prompt: My existing project uses the @dfinity/asset-canister recipe with a .ic-assets.json5 file. How do I make SPA deep-link refreshes work? Just the config.
expected_behaviors: Uses .ic-assets.json5 with enable_aliasing: true for the SPA fallback
Keeps the @dfinity/asset-canister (legacy) recipe rather than forcing a rewrite to static-site
Does NOT tell the user _redirects works on the legacy asset canister

output_evals.name: Mainnet browser-access domain is icp.net
output_evals.prompt: I deployed my static-site frontend canister to mainnet. What URL do I open in the browser to view it? Just the URL pattern.
expected_behaviors: Gives the URL as https://<canister-id>.icp.net
Does NOT use the legacy ic0.app or icp0.io gateway domains
Does NOT use icp-api.io (that is the API endpoint, not the browser gateway)
